findings.title: fsync failures on delta layers no longer abort the process.
findings.body: The old code called `maybe_fatal_err("delta_layer sync_all")`, which aborts the process when fsync fails. That matters because after a failed fsync the page cache can no longer be trusted. The new code turns the failure into an ordinary `DeltaLayerWriterError::Other`. Compaction and flush then retry it and may later upload or use a layer whose durability is unknown, which risks silent data loss. Keep the fatal handling, for example `file.sync_all().await.maybe_fatal_err("delta_layer sync_all").map_err(|e| DeltaLayerWriterError::Other(e.into()))?`.

findings.title: fsync failures on image layers no longer abort the process.
findings.body: This is the same regression as in the delta layer. `maybe_fatal_err("image_layer sync_all")` used to abort on an fsync error, and now the error becomes a retryable `ImageLayerWriterError::Other`. Image layer creation can then retry and keep going after an fsync failure, even though the dirty pages may already be lost. Restore the `maybe_fatal_err` call before mapping the error.

findings.title: The LSN-ordering invariant assert is now a recoverable error.
findings.body: Before this change, `assert!(self.lsn_range.start <= lsn)` panicked when a value was written below the layer's LSN range. That catches a logic bug that could otherwise produce a corrupt layer. It now returns `Other`, and callers treat that as a retryable compaction or flush failure, which hides the bug. Nothing in the request asks for this change. Keep the assert.

findings.title: The new Cancelled variant is turned back into a generic error, so issue #11762 is not fixed.
findings.body: The issue asks that `create image layers: flush task cancelled` stop being reported as a compaction ERROR and retried. This PR adds a typed `Cancelled` variant, but every caller maps it straight back to `anyhow!("flush task cancelled")` inside `CreateImageLayersError::Other`, `CompactionError::Other`, `Error::Prepare`, and so on. The same happens here, in compaction.rs, batch_split_writer.rs, inmemory_layer.rs and detach_ancestor.rs. Callers still see a generic failure, so the compaction loop still logs it at ERROR level and retries it during shutdown. Map `Cancelled` to the cancellation or shutdown variants that already exist (for example `CreateImageLayersError::Cancelled` and `CompactionError::ShuttingDown`).

findings.title: The string-matching error mapping does nothing useful and drops the error's context.
findings.body: Both branches produce `CompactionError::Other`, so `e.to_string().contains("flush task cancelled")` changes nothing about the error's kind. When the message does match, the original error and its context chain are thrown away and replaced by a bare `anyhow!("flush task cancelled")`. The same pattern appears at lines 2240-2246, 3750-3756 and 3769-3775. Those later sites also remove the `.context("failed to finish ... writer")` that was there before. This looks like an abandoned attempt at classifying the error. Match on typed variants, or keep the plain `map_err(CompactionError::Other)` with its context.

findings.title: Formatting the error into a string drops the I/O error's source chain.
findings.body: `.context("get file metadata to determine size")` kept the `io::Error` as the source of the new error. `anyhow!("...: {}", e)` only keeps its message text, so error kinds and nested causes are lost for anyone who downcasts or prints with `{:#}`. The same happens at image_layer.rs lines 1045-1050. Use `anyhow::Error::new(e).context("...")` instead.

findings.title: A closed gate is reported as Other instead of Cancelled.
findings.body: `gate.enter()` fails only when the gate is closing, which means the timeline is shutting down. This is the same shutdown condition the issue is about. Mapping it to `BlobWriterError::Other` means a writer created during shutdown still produces a generic error instead of a cancellation. Map the gate error to `BlobWriterError::Cancelled`.
